## Cleaned inputs for exploratory checks

The workbooks contain respondent-level records and are used locally. The rendered report shows only aggregate output; the RQ3 models are reproduced from the authorised ABS files as described in [Rosetta's methods and results](rq3-rosetta-methods-results.md).

```{r load-data, include=FALSE}
library(readxl)
general <- read_excel("rq3_general_nnpas_cleaned.xlsx", sheet = "eligible_sample")
indigenous <- read_excel("rq3_indigenous_natsinpas_cleaned.xlsx", sheet = "eligible_sample")
```

## Confounders

The extended model adjusts for age, sex, energy intake, SEIFA disadvantage, income decile, Year 12 completion, smoking, and alcohol. The core-covariate sensitivity omits income and Year 12 to retain respondents with those fields missing. See Rosetta's methods for variable definitions and the reason for this comparison.

## Rosetta — fibre, physical activity, and obesity

The [primary model script](rq3-rosetta-main.R) uses Day 1 intake and the surveys' person weights. The [short handoff](rq3-Rosetta-handoff.md) shows which files to use; the [methods and results](rq3-rosetta-methods-results.md) explain the populations and limitations. NNPAS is a general-population sample, **not** a verified non-Indigenous sample. The NATSINPAS activity sample is non-remote. All analyses shown here restrict age to 18–65.

The table reads aggregate CSVs generated by the scripts. The second and third rows use exactly the same Day 2 completers; the third row is the previously submitted two-day analysis.

```{r rosetta-interaction, echo=FALSE}
get_interaction <- function(file, pa_definition = NULL) {
  d <- read.csv(file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  d <- d[grepl("ratio of odds ratios", d$estimate, ignore.case = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!is.null(pa_definition)) d <- d[d$pa_definition == pa_definition, , drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(nrow(d) == 2)
  fmt <- function(r) sprintf("n=%s; %.3f (%.3f–%.3f), p=%.3f",
                             format(r$n, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE),
                             r$odds_ratio, r$ci_low, r$ci_high, r$p_value)
  c(fmt(d[grepl("General", d$group), ]), fmt(d[grepl("Indigenous", d$group), ]))
}
rows <- rbind(
  get_interaction("rq3-rosetta-model.csv", "EXREGUIC"),
  get_interaction("rq3-rosetta-day1-in-day2-model.csv"),
  get_interaction("rq3-rosetta-two-day-model.csv")
)
comparison <- data.frame(
  Analysis = c("All eligible Day 1 respondents — primary",
               "Day 2 completers, Day 1 intake",
               "Day 2 completers, two-day mean"),
  `General NNPAS` = rows[, 1],
  `Indigenous NATSINPAS (non-remote)` = rows[, 2],
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(comparison, caption = "Adjusted fibre × activity interaction OR (95% CI) using the 150-minute threshold")
```

The Day 1 primary interactions are close to 1, with confidence intervals spanning 1 in both surveys. The alternative 150-minute-plus-five-session definition and the reduced-confounder model are reported in the methods file and their aggregate CSVs.

General NNPAS (exploratory, unweighted `eligible_sample`):
Boxplots of BMI, waist circumference, and two-day fibre intake. These plots use the cleaned eligible sample rather than the complete-case primary model cohort.
```{r}
check_outliers <- function(data, name) {
  boxplot(data$bmi, main = paste(name, "- BMI"))
  boxplot(data$waist_cm, main = paste(name, "- Waist Circumference"))
  boxplot(data$fibre_2day_avg_g, main = paste(name, "- Fibre Intake"))
}

check_outliers(general, "General")
check_outliers(indigenous, "Indigenous")
```

Missing data check (exploratory, on the cleaned `eligible_sample` sheets):
```{r}
check_missing <- function(data, name) {
  cat("Missingness for", name, ":\n")
  print(colSums(is.na(data)))
  cat("\n")
}

check_missing(general, "General")
check_missing(indigenous, "Indigenous")
```
